terra.problem: The passage does not say whether Abraham received the whole route up front.
The road-trip comparison suggests Abraham was shown the destination after he set out. The passage does not say when God showed him the mountain.
The explanation suggests Abraham got up early because splitting wood was work. The text does not give his reason.
The explanation is generic and ends with a flat observation about the water supply.
The verse does not say there was no staff or that Abraham's hands were full.
The passage does not say Isaac sees anything on the mountain at this point; their arrival at the designated place comes later.
The text does not describe Abraham's answer as calm.
Abraham tells the servants to stay, but the passage does not say they never climb anywhere.
The dinner comparison mentions food other than cookies.
The passage does not say there is no campsite or tent.
The final sentence talks about the card, which Papa Dorin never does.
The angel says he knows Abraham fears God. The passage does not say the angel has no doubt about Abraham at all.
The closing instruction sounds generic and preachy rather than fatherly.
The explanation is flat, and the last sentence merely repeats details without adding anything.
The passage says Abraham sees a ram, but does not say it is the only animal he finds there.
Abraham tells the servants to stay with the donkey, but the passage does not explicitly say they never come up the mountain.
The passage does not say where Nahor lives or how far he is from the mountain.
